MachinesPage.clockSync.note.message: Keeps the guest's clock right after a snapshot or Suspend. Snapshot and Suspend first press the guest's sleep key, so the guest suspends itself, as a laptop does when its lid closes; it wakes once the file is written, and again when the file is loaded, and its clock catches up with the time that passed. A guest that doesn't sleep on the key, such as one without systemd-logind, is saved as it is after up to 10 s. When this is off, a snapshot is a pause the guest can hardly tell, and its clock lags until something sets it.

MachinesPage.keyboard.followNote.now.note: Machines page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout menu when it is This browser's, at every boot, and the browser reports a layout. {{layout}}: that layout's name. Don't set it quotes the menu's first option.

MachinesPage.keyboard.followNote.message: At every boot, this emulator changes the guest's keyboard settings to the layout this browser reports, for the console, X11, and Wayland. MachinesPage.keyboard.followNote.note: Machines page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout menu when it is This browser's, at every boot, and the browser reports no layout now. Don't set it quotes the menu's first option.

MachinesPage.keyboard.setNote.message: At every boot, this emulator changes the guest's keyboard settings to this layout, for the console, X11, and Wayland. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. Choosing Don't set it later leaves the last layout in place.
MachinesPage.keyboard.setNote.note: Machines page, Settings tab: note under the Keyboard layout menu when a layout is chosen. Don't set it quotes the menu's first option.

MachinesPage.adapters.note.message: A machine can have up to {{max}} adapters, each with its own MAC address (eth0, eth1… in the guest, in this order). Adding, removing, or moving one changes the hardware the guest sees, so snapshots taken before can no longer be restored. You can attach, change, or detach a connection while the machine runs, like plugging in a cable. The guest's default route goes through the first adapter that reaches the internet.
MachinesPage.adapters.note.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under the list of adapters. {{max}}: the most adapters (4).

MachinesPage.netConfig.title.message: At every boot, this emulator has the guest's systemd-networkd apply the settings each connection provides.
MachinesPage.netConfig.title.note: Machines page, Network tab: tooltip of Take the connection's settings in the guest.

MachinesPage.netConfig.message: Take the connection's settings in the guest
MachinesPage.netConfig.note: Machines page, Network tab: the label of a box under the adapters.

MachinesPage.netConfig.on.message: At every boot, this emulator has the guest's systemd-networkd use each connection's MTU and search domain, such as MagicDNS's, and DHCP on adapters nothing else sets up. A tailnet's MTU is 1280; at the adapter's 1500, large packets can be lost. The guest must be running systemd version 256 or above. Nothing is written to the guest's disk, so the settings last until the guest shuts down. NetworkManager applies them by itself.
MachinesPage.netConfig.on.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is ticked.

MachinesPage.netConfig.off.message: This emulator leaves the guest's network settings alone. The guest uses each connection's MTU and search domain only if it's set up to. From the next boot, none of this emulator's settings apply.
MachinesPage.netConfig.off.note: Machines page, Network tab: the note under Take the connection's settings in the guest, while it is unticked.

MachinesPage.storage.persist.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Shown only while the storage isn't persistent.

MachinesPage.storage.persist.title.message: Without this, the browser may delete this page's machines, disks and snapshots on its own when the device runs low on space. This asks the browser to keep them until you delete them yourself. The browser decides whether to agree, and may do so without asking you; if it declines, this button stays.
MachinesPage.storage.persist.title.note: Machines page: the browser's storage, in the bar at the page's bottom. Tooltip of Protect from automatic deletion (MachinesPage.storage.persist).

MachinesPage.storage.clear.title.message: Delete the cached parts of URL disks. They will be read from the network again, by a running machine too. The cache is kept at most a week after its last use, and the browser may clear it sooner when space runs short.
